column2: Whether a collision or reaction cell is installed and its operating mode. In standard mode (STD), no cell gas is introduced and the cell acts only as an ion guide. In dynamic reaction cell (DRC) mode, a reactive gas selectively neutralizes specific interferences through ion-molecule reactions. Specific gas types, flow rates and cell voltages are documented in Group 4. Record 'Not installed' where the instrument has no collision/reaction cell.
column6: Not installed | STD (standard mode, no gas) | KED (kinetic energy discrimination, He gas) | DRC (dynamic reaction cell, reactive gas) | KED+DRC | ICP-MS/MS (triple-quadrupole mode) | N/A | None | Other: specify

column6: 20 µm (contiguous, equal to spot size) | 15 µm pitch with 5 µm gap between lines | N/A (spot or line-scan mode)
column10: Together with spot size, this determines whether adjacent lines are contiguous (line spacing = spot size), overlapping (line spacing < spot size), or have gaps (line spacing > spot size).

column2: Gas used to transport ablated aerosol from the ablation cell to the ICP-MS torch, with the procedure-registered target flow rate(s). Flow rates are procedure targets; actual session values may be adjusted within ±10% during tuning.
column6: e.g., 'He, 0.75 l min⁻¹' | 'He: MFC-1 (cell) 0.60 l min⁻¹ + MFC-2 (cup) 0.35 l min⁻¹'
column10: Helium is standard for most UV laser systems due to superior aerosol transport.
column15: Carrier gas flow: 0.6 L/min; species not named (carrier gas identity not stated in Table 1 or text)
column16: He: 0.7 l min⁻¹ (chamber) + 0.1 l min⁻¹ (cup gas)
column17: He (flow rate not stated; carrier gas with N₂ or Ar mixed for sensitivity optimization)
column18: He (flow rate not stated; same system as glass protocol)

column2: Supplementary gas added to the sample-carrying stream between the sample introduction system and the plasma, with its identity and the procedure-registered target flow rate. Record any small nitrogen or hydrogen addition with its own flow, whose unit commonly differs from the make-up flow. Record 'None' explicitly where no supplementary gas is added, to distinguish it from not reported.
column6: e.g., 'Ar make-up gas, 0.95 l min⁻¹' | 'Ar make-up 0.80 l min⁻¹ + N₂ 2 ml min⁻¹ (sensitivity enhancement)' | 'None (no N₂ added)'
column10: Argon make-up is standard and maintains total gas delivery where the carrier flow alone is insufficient — downstream of an ablation cell, or of a desolvation system that has removed solvent load. Small nitrogen or hydrogen additions enhance sensitivity for some elements.
column15: Ar make-up: 0.9–1.2 l min⁻¹; Ar auxiliary: 0.6–1.2 l min⁻¹
column16: N (gas not separately specified beyond total plasma flow)
column17: N₂ or Ar mixed into He carrier for sensitivity optimization (amounts not stated)
column18: N₂ or Ar mixed (same protocol as glass)

column2: Flow rate of the outer (coolant/plasma) argon gas stream that sustains the ICP plasma, in L/min.
column6: 14 L/min | 15 L/min | Other: specify
column10: Determines plasma volume and stability.
column15: Cool gas: 12–13 l min⁻¹ Ar; Auxiliary: 0.6–1.2 l min⁻¹
column16: Plasma gas flow: 15 l min⁻¹; Auxiliary gas: 0.85 l min⁻¹

column2: Flow rate of the intermediate (auxiliary) argon gas stream, between the torch body and the injector tube, which positions the plasma relative to the load coil, in L/min. Distinct from the outer coolant (plasma) gas and from the gas stream that carries sample into the plasma.
column6: 0.8 L/min | 1.0 L/min | 1.2 L/min | Other: specify
column10: Affects ion extraction efficiency and oxide production rates.

column2: Radiofrequency forward power applied to the ICP, in watts.
column10: Affects plasma temperature, ionisation efficiency, oxide formation, and whether cool or normal plasma conditions are in effect.

column2: Whether the ICP plasma is operated under cool plasma (<=900 W RF) or normal (hot) plasma (>1000 W RF) conditions. Document independently of the RF Power field.
column6: Normal plasma (>1000 W RF) | Cool plasma (≤900 W RF) | Mixed: specify mode per analytical sub-run | N/A | None | Other: specify
column10: Cool plasma substantially reduces argide-based polyatomic interferences (e.g., ⁴⁰Ar on ⁴⁰Ca, ⁴⁰Ar⁴⁰Ar on ⁸⁰Se). A fundamental method design choice that determines which interference corrections are necessary.

column2: Description of any signal smoothing device or approach installed between the ablation cell and the ICP-MS to reduce pulse-to-pulse signal variability. For mapping analyses, report "None" explicitly.
column6: e.g., 'Squid 2.0 (laurin technik)' | 'ARIS (Aerosol Rapid Introduction System)' | 'None'
column10: Note: active signal smoothing devices (e.g., squid, SCFAST) are generally incompatible with high-resolution raster mapping because they degrade spatial resolution by mixing aerosol from successive laser shots.
column17: N (CetacAnalyte HE; smoothing status not reported)

column2: Description of the approach used to optimise ICP plasma conditions prior to analysis, including the reference material used for tuning and the acceptance criteria (e.g., oxide production threshold, sensitivity targets, mass calibration).
column6: e.g., 'Daily auto-tune on NIST SRM 612; optimised for max sensitivity on ¹³⁹La and ²³²Th with ThO⁺/Th⁺ <0.5% and U/Th = 1.0 ± 0.05'
column16: Gas flows optimized via spot ablation of NIST SRM 612 to obtain maximum signal intensities while maintaining ThO/Th <0.3% and U/Th at 0.95–1.05

column2: Instrument sensitivity achieved in the session, with the isotope or channel it was measured on and the conditions it applies to. May be expressed either as detected signal per unit concentration or per unit mass of analyte delivered — counts per second per ppb, volts per ppm, counts per picogram — or as useful yield, the percentage of sampled atoms ultimately detected as ions, with the method used to derive it cited. A sensitivity the procedure requires before analyses may begin belongs with the tuning acceptance criteria.
column6: e.g., '0.42% useful yield (U, method of Horstwood et al. 2016)' | '0.1% useful yield (analytes, msfs-LA-ICP-MS)' | '1.2 x 10^6 cps/ppb on 115In' | 'N/A'
column10: Useful yield is the more comparable of the two wherever the amount of material consumed varies between procedures, as it does with spot size, fluence and repetition rate.

column2: Method used to quantify plasma oxide production and the acceptance threshold applied before commencing analysis. Record both the monitored mass ratio(s) and the maximum allowed threshold(s). Measured values are recorded in Oxide Production. The monitored ratio is procedure-dependent: ThO+/Th+ (m/z 248/232), UO+/U+ (254/238), CeO+/Ce+ (156/140) and BaO+/Ba+ are all in use.

Measured oxide production ratio obtained during session-start tuning, for the proxy specified in Oxide Production Method and Threshold. Record the measured value and confirm whether the procedure threshold was met.
column6: e.g., 'ThO⁺/Th⁺ = 0.3% (threshold <0.5% met)' | 'ThO⁺/Th⁺ = 0.08%' | 'CeO⁺/Ce⁺ = 0.7% (threshold <1.0% met)'
column16: ThO/Th = measured at <0.3%; U/Th = 0.95–1.05 (on NIST SRM 612)

column2: The mass ratio monitored to estimate doubly-charged ion (M²⁺) formation during instrument tuning. The monitor species and the mass positions monitored should be stated explicitly. Analogous to Oxide Production Method and Threshold for oxide monitoring.
column6: ¹³⁸Ba²⁺/¹³⁸Ba⁺ (m/z 69/138); Ce²⁺/Ce⁺ (m/z 70/140); ²³⁸U²⁺/²³⁸U⁺ (m/z 119/238)
column10: Doubly-charged ions appear at half the mass of the parent ion and can cause isobaric interferences on analytes in that mass region.

column2: Measured percentage of doubly-charged ion production for the monitored species at the time of instrument tuning. The acceptable threshold is typically <1% or <3%. Report both the threshold and the measured value where possible.
column6: <1% (threshold); 0.4% (measured, ¹³⁸Ba²⁺/¹³⁸Ba⁺); N (not reported)

column2: Minimum warm-up time required after plasma ignition before analyses begin, and any maximum session duration enforced to maintain stable operating conditions.
column6: e.g., '≥30 min warm-up after sample change; sessions ≤8 h after tuning' | '3–4 h warm-up; no session duration limit'

column2: The repeating order in which calibration or bracketing standards, quality-control and secondary reference materials, blanks and unknowns are interleaved within a measurement session. Adjustments must maintain the bracketing strategy defined in the procedure.
column6: e.g., '1 primary std / 1 QC / 10 unknowns' | '2/4/15' | 'Calibration at start and end; unknowns in between'
column15: IVB meteorite standards (Warburton Range external + Tawallah Valley secondary) measured alongside unknowns; exact bracketing not described
column16: Gas blank (25 s) → ablation (45 s) → washout (25 s); NIST 612 and 614 as external standards; BHVO-2 and 6 GRMs measured as unknowns
column17: NIST 610 as primary standard measured in session; NIST 612 and BCR-2G as monitoring standards; unknowns bracketed by standards
column18: Same bracketing as silicate glass protocol
column19: NIST 610 glass standard analyzed before and after every session; unknowns in between [P4]

column2: The chemical species this procedure is designed to determine, recorded at whatever resolution the chemistry is resolved — element(s) for this technique; valence species where a procedure resolves oxidation state; compounds where it resolves molecules. Isotopes are not analytes: isotopes of an element are the same chemical species. The subset actually measured may be narrower than the registered suite where species were excluded due to interferences or scope reduction.
column6: e.g., 'Major elements: Mg, Si, Ca, Fe; Trace elements: Sc, V, Cr ... U' | 'All REE: La-Lu'
column15: ⁵⁹Co, ¹⁰¹Ru, ¹⁰³Rh, ¹⁰⁵Pd, ¹⁸⁵Re, ¹⁸⁹Os, ¹⁹³Ir, ¹⁹⁵Pt, ¹⁹⁷Au (9 HSE isotopes); ²⁴Mg, ²⁹Si, ³¹P, ³³S monitored for inclusion detection; ⁶¹Ni as internal standard
column16: ²¹Sc, ⁵¹V, ⁵²Cr, ⁵⁹Co, ⁶⁰Ni, ⁶³Cu, ⁶⁶Zn, ⁶⁹Ga, ⁸⁵Rb, ⁸⁸Sr, ⁸⁹Y, ⁹⁰Zr, ⁹³Nb, ¹³³Cs, ¹³⁷Ba, ¹³⁹La, ¹⁴⁰Ce, ¹⁴¹Pr, ¹⁴⁶Nd, ¹⁴⁷Sm, ¹⁵³Eu, ¹⁵⁷Gd, ¹⁵⁹Tb, ¹⁶³Dy, ¹⁶⁵Ho, ¹⁶⁶Er, ¹⁶⁹Tm, ¹⁷²Yb, ¹⁷⁵Lu, ¹⁷⁸Hf, ¹⁸¹Ta, ²³²Th, ²³⁸U (32 trace elements)
column17: ¹⁹⁷Au, ⁶³Cu (primary targets); all detected via Agilent 7900 (exact isotope list not fully stated)
column18: ¹⁹⁷Au, ⁶³Cu (primary targets; Si and Fe from EMP as internal standards)
column19: N (not explicitly listed in methods; results text mentions Sc, V, Ti, Co, Ni, REEs measured in silicates; full isotope list not stated) [P4, P7, P11]
column20: N (not explicitly listed in methods; merrillite REE La-Lu at 14–414 ppm range mentioned in results; full isotope list not stated) [P12]

column2: Specific masses monitored in this procedure, grouped by the analyte element they serve where they serve one. Covers atomic isotopes and, where a reaction cell shifts an analyte onto a different mass, the product mass actually measured. Includes interference-monitor and internal-standard masses, which serve no analyte and so have no parent element. The analyte list is given by the Analyte field and is never inferred from the element symbols appearing here.
column6: ⁷Li | ²⁵Mg | ⁵⁶Fe | ²⁰⁸Pb | (176+82)Hf (NH3 mass-shift product) | N/A | None | Other: specify

column2: The final variable(s) this procedure reports and their units — distinct from the fields recording what was *acquired* rather than what is reported. Record every reported variable, including intermediate quantities reported alongside final ones (e.g. both the 206Pb/238U ratio and the 206Pb/238U date). Where a reported variable is a nominal property with no magnitude (e.g. a mineral identification), record the variable and give the unit as 'N/A — nominal property'.
column6: e.g., 'Element concentrations in ug/g; 2SE per analyte' | '207Pb/206Pb, 206Pb/238U, 207Pb/235U (radiogenic, common-Pb corrected), absolute ratios with 2-sigma'
column10: A procedure may acquire many channels and report a small number of derived quantities; without this field a data consumer cannot tell which.

column2: Mode used to collect ion signal across the monitored masses. In peak hopping mode, the quadrupole jumps sequentially between pre-set mass positions and dwells at each peak; in scanning mode, the quadrupole sweeps continuously across a defined mass range.
column6: Peak hopping | Scanning | N/A | None | Other: specify
column10: Peak hopping is standard for multi-element trace analysis as it maximises integration time at each mass.

column2: Dead time of each ion-counting detector channel, used in the dead-time correction applied to high count rates. Distinct from pulse/analog cross-calibration, which relates the two detector modes rather than correcting counting losses within the pulse-counting mode.
column6: e.g., '23' | '23 ns (determined from NIST 612 at varying spot size, checked quarterly)'

column2: Type of collision gas introduced into the collision/reaction cell in KED mode. Record 'None' if the cell is in STD mode, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include KED or the instrument has no cell.
column6: He | H2 | He+H2 | N/A | None
column10: Helium (He) is the standard collision gas for kinetic energy discrimination, being low in mass and chemically inert.

column2: Flow rate of the collision gas, typically He, introduced into the collision/reaction cell in KED mode, in mL/min. Record 'None' if the cell is in STD mode, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include KED or the instrument has no cell.
column6: 3.5 mL/min | 4.0 mL/min | None (STD mode)
column10: Controls the degree of ion thermalization and KED efficiency; higher flow rates give greater interference suppression at the cost of analyte sensitivity.

column2: Bias voltage applied at the collision/reaction cell exit to discriminate between analyte ions and low-energy polyatomic interferences in KED mode, in volts (V). Record 'None' if the cell is in STD mode, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include KED or the instrument has no cell.
column6: −5 V | −8 V | None (STD mode)
column10: A negative bias preferentially retards slow polyatomic ions while transmitting faster analyte ions, controlling the degree of polyatomic suppression.

column2: Type of reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC) for interference removal through ion-molecule reactions. Common reaction gases include NH₃ (e.g., for Fe, Ca, K isotopes), O₂ (e.g., for As, Ge) and CH₄. Record 'None' if DRC mode is not used, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include DRC or the instrument has no cell.
column6: NH3 | O2 | CH4 | N/A | None

column2: Flow rate of the reactive gas introduced into the dynamic reaction cell (DRC), in mL/min. Record 'None' if DRC mode is not used, and 'N/A' where Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configuration does not include DRC or the instrument has no cell.
column6: 0.4 mL/min | 0.8 mL/min | None

column2: Where the collision or reaction cell is supplied with a mixture of gases rather than a single gas, the identities and proportions of that mixture. Recorded separately from the gas identity. Record 'N/A' where a single gas is used.
column6: e.g., 'NH3:He 1:9' | 'High-purity NH3, no mixture' | 'N/A (single gas)' | 'None'
column10: The proportions change reaction efficiency and interference suppression independently of which gases are used.

column2: Where a monitored mass is produced by a reaction in the collision/reaction cell, the precursor ion, the reagent gas and the product ion measured. Records the mass-shift chemistry relating the mass measured to the analyte it reports, which the monitored mass alone does not state. Record 'N/A' where the analyte is measured on its own mass.
column6: e.g., '176Hf + NH3 -> (176+82)Hf+ (adduct, +82 u)' | 'N/A (on-mass measurement)'

column2: Count time (dwell time) per mass position, in milliseconds.
column6: e.g., 6 ms (most isotopes); 35 ms (¹⁴⁷Sm, ¹⁵³Eu, ¹⁵⁸Gd for REE work)
column10: Longer dwell times improve counting statistics and lower detection limits but reduce the number of isotopes measurable within a given scan cycle time. For mapping, scan cycle time directly determines spatial resolution at a given scan speed: shorter cycle time = finer spatial resolution.
column16: 30 ms (most isotopes) / 10 ms (alternate; dual detector mode)

column1: Total Integration Time per Output Data Point
column2: Total duty-cycle time for one complete mass-scan sweep — the sum of all per-isotope dwell times plus inter-mass settling times. Not recoverable from Dwell Time per Mass alone, because settling time is not captured there. Applies to sequential (quadrupole and single-collector sector-field) acquisition.
column6: e.g., '0.284' | '0.31 s (24 masses, 10 ms dwell, 4 ms settling)'
column10: Sets the time resolution of the downhole signal.

column2: Total time spent measuring gas blank (background signal with laser off or shutter closed) before each ablation event, in seconds. For spot and transect analysis, a discrete background interval is measured before each ablation. For mapping, background is typically measured once per raster line or at the start of a map session rather than before each individual pixel. Editable to allow session-specific adjustment.
column6: e.g., '30 s (spot/transect)' | '10 s per raster line (mapping)' | '25 s (one gas blank map per GRM at session start)'
column16: 25 s gas blank before each ablation
column17: N (gas blank measured but duration not explicitly stated)
column19: 50 s (background counted for 50 s before each LA-ICP-MS analysis) [P4]

column2: Whether the procedure uses a single acquisition pass or multiple sequential runs on the same sample location, each optimized for different analytical objectives. For multi-run designs, describe the number of runs, their purpose, key laser and instrument settings per run, and how outputs of one run feed into data reduction of another. Not applicable to raster mapping, where each spatial location is visited exactly once.
column6: e.g., Single run | Two sequential runs: run 1 (major elements, 30 µm circular, medium resolution) → run 2 (trace elements, 130 µm circular, low resolution; Cr from run 1 as IS) | Pre-ablation pass + single acquisition run
column15: Single spot per location (30 µm circular)
column16: Single spot per location (45 s ablation at 1 Hz)
column17: Single spot per location (~40 s ablation at 7 Hz)
column18: Single spot per location (sulfides; same acquisition parameters as glass but 20 µm spot)

column2: Location of the analysis on the sample surface. For spot and transect analysis: stage coordinates (X, Y in µm) or a description relative to a named reference feature (e.g., mineral rim, inclusion boundary). For mapping: coordinates of the map corner(s) or centre, plus map dimensions.
column6: e.g., 'X = 12350 µm, Y = 8760 µm (stage coordinates)' | '500 µm from metal-olivine rim toward core' | 'Map centre: X=15000, Y=9000 µm; area: 1450×600 µm'
column10: Enables spatial reconstruction and co-registration with other analytical images.

column2: Number of replicate measurements performed on the same sample, or on the same nominal location where the technique is spatially resolved. For spot analysis this is the number of individual spots per grain or location; for transects, the number of replicate lines; for mapping, the number of map acquisitions of the same area; for solution work, the number of discrete replicate measurements acquired per sample solution.
column6: e.g., 3 (three replicate spots per grain) | 1 (single transect) | 1 (single map)
column15: N (variable number of spots per grain; Mg, Si, P, S monitored to check for inclusions)
column16: 9 spot analyses in grid pattern for homogeneity testing; multiple analyses per fusion glass disk
column18: N (grain size >20 µm selected; number of analyzed grains variable)

column2: Total length of the transect line analysed in micrometres. Scan speed is captured separately in Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size.
column10: Depends on the size of the feature of interest rather than being fixed in the procedure.

column2: Total area covered by the 2D raster map, expressed as width × height in µm or as total area in µm² or mm². This is an analysis-level parameter because it depends on the size of the grain or phase to be mapped. The procedure fixes scan speed, line spacing, and spot size; the map area is chosen at analysis time to cover the target feature.
Method used to determine the internal standard (IS) concentration for each unknown sample.
column6: e.g., 'Single element from EPMA (SiO₂ wt% used as IS)' | 'Sum-of-major-oxide normalization to 100% (Liu et al. 2008)' | 'Stoichiometry-derived (Ca fixed at 10.1 wt% for calcite)' | 'No IS — external calibration only'
column10: Corrects for variable ablation yield between analyses.
column15: Single element externally measured by EPMA: ⁶¹Ni concentration from EPMA at exact analysis location used as IS
column16: Two internal standards: Si from XRF SiO₂ (for Co, Ni, Cu, Zn); Al from XRF Al₂O₃ (for all other trace elements); non-matrix-matched external standards (NIST 612 + 614) used; fs laser minimizes matrix effects
column17: Single element from EMP: Si (SiO₂ from EMP for silicate glass); NIST 610 as external standard
column18: Single element from EMP: Fe (FeOT from EMP for sulfide); NIST 610 as external standard
column19: Normalization to 100 wt% oxide total (for silicates and oxides) [P4]
column20: Single element IS: EMP CaO concentration used; LA-ICP-MS 40Ca counts normalized to CaO from EMP analysis at the same spot [P4]

column2: Element(s) used as the internal standard, the monitored isotope, and how the internal-standard concentration was established for unknowns. Where the element serves isotope-ratio work it must have a known isotopic composition and a mass close to the analyte's. Record 'None' together with the alternative used where no internal standard is applied.
column6: e.g., '²⁹Si; SiO₂ wt% from EPMA' | '⁵³Cr; measured in preceding major-element run (run 1)' | 'None — sum of MgO+FeO+SiO₂+P₂O₅ = 100 wt% (Liu et al. 2008)' | For mapping procedures using oxide-sum normalization, report "None (oxide-sum normalization)" and cite the method reference.
column15: ⁶¹Ni; concentration from EPMA measured at exact analysis spot location
column16: Si (SiO₂ from XRF) for Co, Ni, Cu, Zn; Al (Al₂O₃ from XRF) for all other 28 trace elements
column17: Si from EMP (SiO₂ wt% for silicate glass)
column18: Fe from EMP (FeOT wt% for sulfide)
column20: 40Ca; CaO wt% from EMP at the analysis spot [P4]

column2: Approach used to convert measured ion signals to reported concentrations, and specifically any case where different analytes or analyte groups within one procedure are calibrated differently - different primary standards for different mass ranges or phases, or one element serving as internal standard while others are externally calibrated. Where a single strategy applies to all analytes, record that strategy. Where the procedure reports isotope ratios only and no concentrations, record 'Not applicable (isotope ratios only)'.
column6: Single strategy: ⁴³Ca IS for all analytes (see Internal Standard fields); Multi-strategy: ⁴³Ca IS for major elements; NIST 610 external calibration for REEs; Fe+Ni+Co sum normalization for PGEs

column2: Method used to correct for laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF), including downhole fractionation during prolonged ablation, matrix-dependent fractionation between sample and calibration standard, and any specific correction algorithm applied. Reference the software function or publication.
column6: e.g., 'Normalised to NIST SRM 612; no additional downhole correction' | 'Exponential downhole fractionation correction in Iolite using NIST SRM 612' | 'Linear time-drift correction applied per analysis'
column15: External calibration using calibration curve method with IVB iron meteorite standards; ⁶¹Ni as IS from EPMA corrects for ablation yield differences between sample and standard
column16: Femtosecond laser substantially reduces elemental fractionation and matrix effects (stated); non-matrix-matched external standards (NIST 612 + 614) used successfully with fs laser (verified by GRM accuracy assessment)
column17: Femtosecond laser reduces LIEF; NIST 610 external standard; Si IS from EMP corrects for ablation yield
column18: Femtosecond laser reduces LIEF; NIST 610 external standard; Fe IS from EMP corrects for ablation yield; micronuggets identified from Au signal spikes and excluded from integration
column19: External calibration using NIST 610 glass standard analyzed before and after session; oxide-sum normalization corrects for ablation yield variation; no explicit downhole fractionation correction described [P4]
column20: External calibration using NIST 610; EMP CaO as IS corrects for ablation yield; no explicit downhole correction described [P4]

column2: Strategy used to correct instrumental isotopic mass fractionation, also called mass bias or mass discrimination. Distinct from Elemental Fractionation Correction, which addresses inter-element fractionation during ablation and transport: this field addresses discrimination between isotopes of the same element, and applies wherever the procedure reports isotope ratios.
column6: e.g., 'Standard-sample bracketing against NIST 612' | 'Co-aspirated Tl, exponential law' | 'None (elemental concentrations only)'

column2: The convention at which reported uncertainties are quoted — 1-sigma, 2-sigma, or a 95% confidence interval — and whether a measured spread is reported as a standard error or a standard deviation. State the convention applying to all values reported under this procedure, and state each separately where different reported quantities use different conventions. Distinct from Uncertainty Propagation Method, which addresses how component uncertainties are combined rather than how the result is quoted.
column6: 2σ (95% confidence) | 1σ (68% confidence) | 95% confidence interval | 2 standard errors (2SE) | 1 standard deviation (1SD) | N/A | None
column10: A reported uncertainty is not interpretable without it: the same numeric value means different things at 1-sigma and at 95% confidence.

column2: The approach used to propagate analytical uncertainty through the data reduction chain to the final reported value. State which sources are included in the propagation: counting statistics, calibration standard uncertainty, internal standard uncertainty, drift correction, and any systematic contributions. Distinct from Uncertainty Level, which states the convention at which the resulting uncertainty is quoted.
column6: e.g., Counting statistics only (1σ on integrated signal, Longerich et al. 1996) | SD of n replicate analyses used as combined uncertainty estimate | Full propagation: counting + calibration standard + IS uncertainty (specify formula)

column2: Whether an empirical correction was applied to account for systematic differences in laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF) patterns between the external calibration standard and the sample matrix.
column6: e.g., 'Applied: 6.4% offset in Ca/Si determined by comparison with EPMA (Jenner & O'Neill 2012)' | 'Not applied; Ca used as IS to cancel LIEF offset' | 'Not applicable'
column15: N (fs laser minimizes LIEF; IVB iron meteorite standards used as matrix-matched reference)
column19: N (not stated; agreement within <10% between oxide-sum normalization and EMP-based IS noted as validation) [P4]

column2: Method used to define which portion of the acquired signal is integrated for each reported measurement, and the rule for excluding unstable or anomalous portions. State whether the interval is the full acquisition, a stable sub-interval selected by inspection, or selected by an automated criterion, and name the criterion.
column6: Full acquisition | Stable interval selected by inspection | Automated threshold | Automated outlier rejection | Fixed time window | N/A | None
column15: Time-resolved signals monitored; analyses with elevated Mg, Si, P, S (inclusion indicators) excluded; stable signal intervals used for integration
column16: Time-resolved signals inspected visually; flux blank contributions to pollution elements (V, Co, Zn, Ba, La, Ce, Ta, U) identified and subtracted; 9-spot grid homogeneity tested before analysis
column17: Time-resolved LA-ICP-MS signal inspected; micronuggets identified from spikes in Au signal and excluded from integration to obtain smooth signals (verified by Fig. 1 in paper)
column18: Same approach as glass; micronugget identification from Au signal spikes critical for sulfide analyses
column19: Time-lapse plots of each spot examined; only the plateau region used to quantify trace element abundances [P4]
column20: Time-lapse plots examined; only plateau region used (same as silicate protocol) [P4]

column2: The integration time actually used for the reported signal, in seconds - the time retained after the signal-integration interval has been applied, and therefore equal to or shorter than the total acquisition. Where the procedure computes it from an acquisition structure, record that basis.
column6: e.g., 40 s | 60 s | Not applicable to mapping analysis: for mapping, the equivalent concept is the per-pixel cycle time, determined by the spectrometer dwell time settings.
column10: It is equal to or shorter than the Ablation Duration per Spot because the signal start and end transients are typically discarded.
column16: 45 s on-sample ablation (full ablation interval used for integration)
column17: ~40 s (inferred from typical CetacAnalyte HE protocol; stable signal used)

column2: Criteria used to identify and exclude anomalous data - signal spikes, individual cycles, or whole replicate measurements - before the reported value is calculated. State where in the reduction sequence the filter is applied.
column6: e.g., 'Significant single spikes visually identified and removed in Iolite' | 'Statistical filter: data points >3σ from running mean removed' | 'No filtering applied' | 'Automated spike detection in SILLS'
column15: Monitoring of Mg, Si, P, S to check for micro-inclusions (sulfides); analyses with elevated inclusion signals excluded entirely
column16: Homogeneity index (H) applied to test element distribution; Co, Ni, Cu in high-Si glass (GSR-1) identified as near-LOD and flagged; flux blank contributions to pollution elements subtracted
column17: Micronuggets identified from Au signal spikes in time-resolved spectra; excluded from integration (smooth signals = fully dissolved Au; Fig. 1 shows this criterion)
column18: Same approach as glass; Au spike identification critical for determining solubility vs. nugget contribution
column19: N (not explicitly stated; implied by plateau-region selection excluding non-stable intervals) [P4]

column2: Method used to subtract background and, where relevant, procedural blank from the measured signal. State what is subtracted - instrument background acquired with no sample reaching the plasma, an on-peak zero acquired on the same matrix, or a separately measured procedural blank - over what interval it is measured, and at what granularity it is applied.
column6: Gas blank | On-peak zero | Solution blank | Procedural blank | On-peak zero + procedural blank | N/A | None

column2: Equation or procedure used to calculate and remove each interference contribution, together with how its magnitude was established - a monitor mass measured simultaneously and scaled by natural abundance ratios, a production-rate factor measured on a reference material or interference standard solution, or a tailing factor measured on a pure standard. Name the reference material used.

column2: Mass balance approach used to calculate sample mass fractions, and where applicable isotope ratios, from spike-sample isotope ratio measurements. For double-spike procedures the ratios and concentrations are co-determined through the spike inversion; for conventional isotope dilution the IUPAC ID equations are used. Record 'None' where neither isotope dilution nor double-spike methods are applied.

column2: Procedure applied to identify and minimise carry-over of high-concentration or isotopically distinct material from a preceding measurement into the current one. Mitigation is applied primarily at measurement time, by allowing sufficient washout or rinse between successive introductions. At data processing level, record any flagging or exclusion of measurements where the required washout may not have been achieved.

column2: Post-acquisition normalization applied to the reported data beyond the primary calibration — for example correction to a reference value derived from secondary reference materials, or correction for a systematic bias those materials reveal. Record 'None' if no additional normalization is applied.
column6: e.g., 'None' | '100% oxide sum normalization applied per pixel to enforce mass balance (Liu et al. 2008)' | 'Normalized to ⁸⁸Sr/⁸⁶Sr = 8.37521 for mass bias correction in Sr isotope analysis'

column17: No post-acquisition normalization beyond IS (Si from EMP)
column18: No post-acquisition normalization beyond IS (Fe from EMP)

column20: No post-acquisition normalization; EMP CaO applied directly as IS; NIST 610 for external calibration [P4]

column2: An externally-calibrated factor that converts the measured quantity into the reported quantity, how it was determined, and its uncertainty. Applies where the conversion depends on a factor calibrated against a reference of independently known value, rather than on the instrument response alone. Distinct from the fields that name the calibration material and that state which approach applies to which analyte, where the technique has them: this field records the resulting factor itself.
column6: e.g., ID-TIMS: EARTHTIME ET535 or ET2535 tracer, calibrated per Condon et al. (2015) and McLean et al. (2015), with stated uncertainty | LA-ICP-MS: matrix-matched primary zircon RM of independently known age (91500, GJ-1, Plesovice) used for downhole-fractionation and Pb/U calibration, with the accepted age and its source

column2: The measured level of the analytical blank in the session, and — where the reported quantity is a ratio — its composition, since a blank subtracted from a ratio biases the result unless its own composition is known. Companion to the blank correction method.
column6: e.g., 'Total procedural Pb blank 0.6 +/- 0.3 pg; blank Pb composition 206Pb/204Pb = 18.55, 207Pb/204Pb = 15.50, 208Pb/204Pb = 38.08 (long-term lab average, n = 42)' | 'Gas blank 120 counts/s at mass 206, subtracted per analysis'
column10: Follows the criterion-versus-measurement split the library applies wherever a procedure sets a threshold and an analysis reports a value against it.

column2: The rules determining which individual analyses contribute to a reported aggregate result, together with the outcome of applying them: how many analyses were acquired, how many were included, and on what grounds any were excluded. Distinct from within-analysis outlier filtering, which removes anomalous points inside a single analysis: this field decides which whole analyses enter the reported value.
column6: e.g., '30 grains analysed, 24 included; excluded 4 discordant beyond -5% to +10% and 2 with Pb*/Pbc < 20' | 'All analyses included, no filter applied'
column10: Criteria and outcome are combined in one field because neither is interpretable without the other, following the precision/accuracy precedent.

column2: The equation used to convert the measured quantities into an age or date, together with a citation for that equation. Name the equation unambiguously; where a procedure supports more than one, state which is used and under what conditions. Distinct from Age Model and Software, which records how multiple analyses are combined into a single reported result.
column6: e.g., 206Pb/238U and 207Pb/235U date equations (Jaffey et al. 1971 decay constants) | 207Pb/206Pb date | Wetherill concordia intercept | Tera-Wasserburg concordia intercept | 238U/206Pb-207Pb/206Pb isochron
column10: Required by every geochronology reporting standard surveyed (Condon et al. 2024; Schaen et al. 2021; Rooney et al. 2024; Flowers et al. 2024; Kohn et al. 2024; Mahan et al. 2023).

column2: The kind of date or age the procedure reports. Where more than one type is reported, list all, separated by semicolons.
column6: Weighted mean 206Pb/238U | Weighted mean 207Pb/235U | Weighted mean 207Pb/206Pb | Concordia upper intercept | Concordia lower intercept | Tera-Wasserburg intercept | Single-grain date | Isochron date | Other: specify | N/A | None
column10: Most dating systems derive several different date types from the same measurements, so a reported age is ambiguous without this. Kohn et al. (2024) carry this as a named required item ("fission-track age type"); the equivalent distinction is required by all five other standards surveyed.

column2: How any non-radiogenic, inherited or pre-existing component of the measured signal was accounted for, including the composition assumed, its source, and its uncertainty. Record 'None' where the measured quantity accumulates from zero and no such component exists.
column6: e.g., Stacey & Kramers (1975) two-stage model Pb at the interpreted age | 204Pb-based correction | 207Pb-based correction | 208Pb-based correction | Tera-Wasserburg anchored lower intercept | measured Pb from co-genetic K-feldspar | None (Pb*/Pbc sufficiently high that correction is negligible; state the threshold)
column10: Applies to five of the six dating systems surveyed; fission track is the sole genuine exception, as tracks accumulate from zero. The value actually applied is frequently sample-specific (a two-stage model composition evaluated at the interpreted age) or session-derived (a trapped composition solved from an isochron intercept), so a revision to the assumed composition should not require registering a new procedure. Same reasoning as Rule 5's Constants and Reference Values Used.

column2: The proportion of the measured signal that is radiogenic, as opposed to inherited, initial or otherwise non-radiogenic. Measured companion to Inherited or Initial Signal Correction.
column6: Reported for U-Pb as Pb*/Pbc, the ratio of radiogenic to common Pb. e.g., '1250' | '18' | 'range 12-340 across 24 analyses'
column10: It indicates how strongly the reported age depends on the assumed non-radiogenic composition — a result derived from a low radiogenic fraction is sensitive to that assumption in a way a high-fraction result is not, and that sensitivity is invisible from the age and its uncertainty alone. Follows the criterion-versus-measurement split used for Oxide Production.

column2: The statistical model used to combine individual analyses into a single reported age, including any criteria governing which model is applied. Record the model only — the software implementing it belongs in Data Reduction Software (Group 3), whose scope already extends to age calculation; where reduction and age regression use different packages, list both there.
column6: e.g., Weighted mean with MSWD-based uncertainty expansion | York (1969) regression | IsoplotR Model-1, escalating to Model-3 where MSWD exceeds the stated cutoff | Bayesian / Monte Carlo age model
column10: This is a methodological choice that changes the result: a Model-1 and a Model-3 regression of the same data yield different ages and different uncertainties. Required in some form by all six geochronology reporting standards surveyed.

column2: The zero point from which the reported age is measured, where this is not the present day, and the date it corresponds to. Record 'Present day' where the conventional datum applies. Where the datum is not the present, record it explicitly: year of sample collection for luminescence, end of irradiation for 40Ar/39Ar decay corrections.
column6: Present day (the conventional datum for U-Pb; state explicitly rather than leaving blank)
column10: Required in these cases by Mahan et al. (2023) and Schaen et al. (2021).

column2: Correction for initial disequilibrium in intermediate daughter products of the U decay chains — principally 230Th, and where relevant 231Pa — together with the Th/U or Pa/U partitioning value assumed and its source. Record 'None' with a justification where no correction was applied.
column6: e.g., '230Th correction applied, Th/U(magma) = 2.8 assumed from whole-rock' | '230Th and 231Pa corrections applied (Crowley et al. 2007)' | 'None (sample older than 100 Ma; effect below stated uncertainty)'
column10: Unique to U-Pb among dating systems, because the chains are long enough for intermediate-daughter disequilibrium at crystallisation to bias the 206Pb/238U date, most severely in young samples. Condon et al. (2024) write "we recommend these dates be reported corrected for initial 230Th and 231Pa daughter isotope disequilibrium" — recommended rather than required.

column2: How discordance between the 206Pb/238U, 207Pb/235U and 207Pb/206Pb chronometers is defined for this procedure, and the discordance values obtained. State the formula used. The rule for excluding discordant analyses, and how many were excluded, belong in Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteria.
column6: e.g., '100 x (1 - [206Pb/238U date] / [207Pb/206Pb date])' | '2-sigma concordia ellipse overlap' | 'discordance -3% to +7% across 24 analyses'
column10: Genuinely specific to U-Pb: it is the only system in routine use with two independent decay schemes in the same mineral, so agreement between them is an internal consistency test no other system can run. Condon et al. (2024) write that for samples older than a few hundred million years "it is also useful to provide a measure of discordance" — useful and age-conditional rather than required. Several definitions are in circulation and they are not interchangeable.

column2: The correlation coefficient between pairs of reported quantities whose uncertainties are not independent, together with the pair it applies to and how it was obtained.
column6: e.g., 'rho(206Pb/238U, 207Pb/235U) = 0.83, from the data reduction software error propagation' | 'rho = 0.31 (double-spike inversion covariance)'
column10: Concordia and isochron regressions cannot be reconstructed without it.

column2: Physical constants and reference values used in data reduction to calculate the final reported quantity (e.g., decay constants for age calculation, standard isotope ratios, or other citable reference values used in a correction or calculation), together with their source. Distinct from the Group 6 reference-material fields, which document accepted values for specific calibration/validation materials rather than universal physical constants. Record "None" if no citable, revisable physical constants feed into this procedure's data reduction.

Name and reference material identifier of the primary reference material(s) against which the instrument is calibrated — converting raw signal intensities to concentrations, or anchoring an isotope ratio as the bracketing standard or zero-delta reference. Give the material name, its source or supplier, and a citation for the accepted values used, since results calibrated against different published values for the same material are not directly comparable.

column20: NIST 610 analyzed before and after every session (same as silicate protocol) [P4]

column15: Tawallah Valley (IVB iron meteorite; Walker et al. 2008) — measured as secondary/check standard alongside unknowns

column2: Detection limit, one per reported concentration variable (one per analyte, these being the same set). State the units and whether the values are procedure-typical estimates or session-specific measured values. The calculation method is recorded separately in Detection Limit Method. Record 'N/A' where the procedure reports no concentrations.
column6: e.g., '0.003 ng g⁻¹ (La), 0.005 ng g⁻¹ (Ce) (3σ background; Longerich et al. 1996)' | 'Range: 0.005–23.5 µg g⁻¹ across all measured isotopes (Pettke et al. 2012)'

column17: Detection limits for Au ~0.01 ppm; Cu ~0.1 ppm in silicate melt (stated in paper)
column18: N (detection limits for sulfide not stated; only silicate melt detection limits given as Au ~0.01 ppm, Cu ~0.1 ppm)
column19: Referenced in Table 3 and Table S1; specific values not directly stated in main text; REE in olivines below detection limits at 24–32 µm conditions [P4, P7, P11]
column20: Referenced in Table 3 and Table S1; specific values not directly stated in main text; merrillite REE at 14–414 ppm range above detection [P4, P12]

column2: Formula or approach used to calculate the detection limits, with a citation for the method where one exists. Must be consistent with the values reported in Detection Limit.
column6: 3σ blank | 3σ background | 3σ counting statistics | 3× blank mean | Poisson statistics | N/A | None
column16: Pettke (2012) for most elements: LOD = (3.29 × √(Rbkg × DT × ...) + 2.71) / (Nan × DT × S); LOQ for pollution elements = blank value + 10SD (IUPAC Gold Book)
column17: N (stated as "detection limits" without specific formula)

column2: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the limit of quantification (LOQ): the lowest concentration reliably measurable with acceptable precision and accuracy. Mandatory at analysis level when concentrations near the LOD are reported.
column6: 10σ blank | 10σ background | 10× LOD | 3.3× LOD | S/N ≥ 10 | N/A | None
column10: Concentrations between LOD and LOQ are detectable but not reliably quantifiable.
column16: LOQ = 3.3 × LOD per Pettke (2012) for most elements; LOQ = blank value + 10SD per IUPAC Gold Book for pollution elements (V, Co, Zn, Ba, La, Ce, Ta, U) where blank contribution is significant

column2: Uncertainty predicted from counting statistics — the theoretical limit set by the Poisson distribution of the counts accumulated — for each reported quantity per analysis, with the sigma level stated. Derived from the counts on the analyte together with those on any background or blank subtracted from it. Distinct from the scatter actually observed within a measurement or between repeated measurements, which is recorded separately.
column6: e.g., '2SE predicted from counting statistics over 45 cycles' | '~0.6% (1 sigma), counting statistics plus propagated uncertainties' | 'N/A'
column9: sample > sampling unit x reported property
column10: Where a procedure reports both, agreement indicates the measurement is shot-noise limited, and a larger observed scatter indicates a further source of variance.

column1: Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
column2: Precision of a single measurement, derived from the scatter of the cycles, sweeps or integrations that make it up, together with the method used to assess it. State the statistic (2SE, 2SD, 1s RSD), the number of cycles it is computed over, and the reported quantity it applies to. Distinct from Counting Statistics Error, which records the uncertainty predicted from the counts rather than the scatter observed; where a procedure reports both, record the observed value here and the predicted value there.
column6: e.g., '2SE = 2SD/sqrt(n), n = 45 cycles' | '+/-0.001-0.002 (2SE) on 206Pb/204Pb' | '~2.6% (2SE) on single-spot ages' | 'N/A'
column9: sample > sampling unit x reported property
column10: This is the finest of the three precision levels the library records, below within-session and between-session precision: it describes the repeatability of one analysis rather than agreement between analyses, and is normally the smallest of the three.

column1: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
column2: Precision of repeated measurements within a single analytical session and the method used to assess it. Report both the assessment method and the precision values. The assessment method must specify the reference material or standard measured, the number of replicates n, and the statistic reported (1s RSD, 2s RSD, 2SD, 2SE, 95% CI). Distinct from the internal precision of a single measurement, which derives from counting statistics over the cycles of that measurement rather than from repeated analyses.
column6: e.g., '1σ RSD = 1.5% for Ba, 2.3% for La (n=5 on NIST SRM 612 per session)' | 'Mapping: 4% 1σ RSD across 3 GRM map areas at session start and end (n=3)'
column15: Analytical uncertainties: 2SE of individual spot measurements reported alongside data
column16: Analytical precision (RSD) within 10% for most of 32 trace elements in 6 silicate GRMs (verified by homogeneity index assessment across 9 spots per disk)

column1: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
column2: Precision of measurements across multiple analytical sessions over weeks to months — long-term or intermediate precision — and the method used to assess it. Report both the assessment method and the precision values, specifying the reference material, the number of measurements and sessions, the time span covered, and the statistic reported.
column6: e.g., '2σ RSD = 3% for Eu/Eu* on GOR132-G across 12 sessions over 8 months' | '1σ RSD = 2% for most REEs on BHVO-2G across 17 sessions over 3 years (n=85 analyses)'
column10: Long-term precision is normally poorer than within-session precision and is the figure a data user should carry when comparing results from different sessions.

column2: Offset between measured and accepted values for secondary reference materials, and the method used to assess it. Specify the reference material and the source of its accepted values, the number of analyses, and the quantities assessed. Report systematic biases and their likely causes. Express the offset in the form appropriate to what the procedure reports - percent relative bias for concentrations, or deviation in delta or ratio units for isotopic quantities.
column6: e.g., 'Within ±5% of GeoReM preferred values for most REEs on GOR132-G (n=15); +8% for Nb (known matrix sensitivity)' | '±3% for all elements on BHVO-2G vs. GeoReM (n=20)'
column15: N (accuracy formally assessed by comparison with internal standard; absolute accuracy not separately reported)
column16: Analytical results within 10% of reference values for most of 32 trace elements in 6 GRMs (mafic to felsic); precision (RSD) within 10% for most elements; lunar basalt (NWA14526) and shergottite (NWA13190) results compared with SN-ICP-MS and found reliable
column17: Au and Cu fully dissolved in most glasses (smooth signals); Au results consistent with Au solubility trends from literature; comparison with SN-ICP-MS (solution) for two extraterrestrial samples confirms reliability
column18: Sulfide Au and Cu concentrations consistent with strong positive correlation with log fS₂ (Fig. 5A) confirming thermodynamic equilibrium; partitioning coefficients Dsulfide/melt consistent with literature (Li et al. 2019, 2021)
column19: For silicates: oxide-sum normalization agrees within <10% with EMP-based IS method (internal cross-check, not a separate QC standard) [P4]
column20: N (no accuracy assessment stated for phosphate protocol) [P4]

column2: The statistic reported to show whether scatter among the contributing analyses exceeds what analytical uncertainty alone predicts, together with its value. The procedure may still state an acceptance threshold, which belongs with the inclusion criteria.
column6: e.g., 'MSWD = 1.13 (n = 24), probability of fit 0.31' | 'MSWD = 4.2; excess scatter attributed to protracted crystallisation, Model-3 regression applied'
column10: Answers whether a reported aggregate is defensible as a single population. The value cannot be known before the analysis.

column2: Any procedure- or analysis-specific information not captured by a structured field anywhere in this TAPP — including anomalies, deviations from the registered procedure, instrument modifications, and supplementary context. Scope is the whole document, not Group 6: this is the last field of the TAPP and covers all six groups. Use sparingly; a structured field is preferred for anything that can be formally categorised.
column15: fs laser (260 nm Ti:sapphire) essential for HSE measurement in metal (reduces elemental fractionation and matrix effects); IVB iron meteorite standards (Warburton Range + Tawallah Valley) as matrix-matched standards for iron meteorite metal
column16: Target: bulk trace element analysis of extraterrestrial samples using only 10 mg; Li-borate flux fusion (35:1 dilution) with fs laser — first reported use of fs laser for flux fusion glass analysis; non-matrix-matched external standards demonstrated accurate with fs laser
column17: Analysis of quenched experimental glasses from high-pressure (1 GPa) piston-cylinder experiments; Au and Cu solubility measurements; smooth time-resolved signals indicate fully dissolved Au (no micronuggets)
column18: Analysis of quenched experimental pyrrhotite (Fe₁₋ₓS) from same piston-cylinder experiments; 20 µm spot required due to small grain size (5–50 µm); same instrument and analytical session as glass protocol
column19: Paper broadly follows Udry et al. (2012) and Pernet-Fisher et al. (2014) for procedure; two IS approaches used for different mineral phases (oxide-sum for silicates; EMP CaO for phosphate); 90 µm spot used on some olivines to evaluate whether low REE signals result from insufficient sampling volume [P4]
column20: N/A — see silicate column for general notes [P4]
